page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-192-lssd is a high-density instance configuration featuring 192 dedicated vCPUs based on x86_64 architecture paired with 1512 GB of system memory. Operating at approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance provides a substantial memory envelope alongside high parallel compute capability. The configuration does not include discrete hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Integrated local storage is a defining characteristic of this type, providing 6442 GB of direct-attached NVMe solid-state storage distributed across 16 local SSDs. This integrated disk architecture offers massive local storage throughput and low-latency disk I/O directly attached to the host, bypassing the latency overhead associated with network-attached block storage volumes. Public IPv4 addresses are not bundled by default and must be provisioned separately.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the resource density of 192 vCPUs combined with 1.5 TB of memory and integrated local NVMe storage reduces the operational overhead of running multi-node clusters for data-intensive processing. The bundled NVMe drives offer significant local throughput without the continuous per-IOPS or provisioning charges common to network storage, though workloads must handle disk ephemerality.

The c4d-highmem-192-lssd is suited for massive in-memory databases, large distributed database nodes, high-performance transactional systems, big data analytics engines, and intensive ETL pipelines requiring both rapid memory operations and high-throughput temporary or scratch storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-192-lssd is an x86_64 instance engineered for memory-intensive and I/O-heavy processing. It provides 192 dedicated vCPUs and 1512 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory allocation of approximately 7.88 GB per vCPU. Storage performance is anchored by an integrated 6442 GB NVMe array composed of 16 local SSDs, delivering high local disk throughput with minimal latency. With no discrete GPUs included, compute and memory density remain the primary architectural focus. This high resource density enables consolidation of large enterprise workloads that would otherwise require multiple nodes. Cost efficiency is emphasized through bundled high-speed local disk capacity, eliminating external storage protocol overhead for intermediate data. The instance is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, intensive ETL pipelines, and high-throughput transactional database systems.
